newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHEARER'S FIRST HAT-TRICK RESCUES NEWCASTLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHEARER'S FIRST HAT-TRICK RESCUES NEWCASTLE.

text.p: Just when it seemed Newcastle's leaky defence would cost them three valuable points, England striker Alan Shearer's remarkable late hat-trick salvaged their premier league title ambitions on Sunday.

The 15 million pounds ($24 million) transfer's first hat-trick since he joined Newcastle at the start of this season overturned a 3-1 deficit they faced with 13 minutes remaining and gave them a 4-3 triumph over a Leicester City side who themselves had scored three in 13 minutes of the second half.

Newcastle's victory boosted them to within five points of leaders Manchester United, who won 2-1 at home against Southampton on Saturday, but Shearer was the first to admit they had done it the hard way.
"We keep giving ourselves a mountain to climb," he said after netting the winner almost two minutes into injury time.
The victory came on the heels of a 4-1 victory over Everton on Wednesday in which they surrendered the opening goal.
"That's Newcastle United. When you come here you get entertainment, but we'd much prefer to win 1-0 or 2-1 rather than having to do it the hard way," Shearer said.
Newcastle led at half-time on Robbie Elliot's fourth-minute goal but Shearer said: "You're never comfortable at 1-0, especially in the Premiership.

"We had the chances to go in more up and perhaps we should have. We felt comfortable at half-time but give them credit, they've ruffled us a bit and played some tremendous football and scored some good goals.
"But just like against Everton in midweek we never put our heads down, we kept going and we got our reward.
"We've got belief here that we are good enough to win matches and no disrespect to Leicester but we should be winning games like this, especially at home."
They remained fourth in the table. "We had to win really to keep in touch. Arsenal dropped a couple of points yesterday but Liverpool and Man United both won so it was important."
New manager Kenny Dalglish, who took over from Kevin Keegan last month, was delighted by the victory but said: "Games like this are probably why Kevin went grey."
Dalglish felt the title race would go down to the wire. "I don't think there'll be too many issues decided until the final week," he said."
Leicester's second half goals came from Matt Elliott, Steve Claridge and Emile Heskey.

Shearer threw Newcastle a lifeline with one of his freekick specials in the 77th minute, drilled home an equaliser from 18 yards seven minutes from time and tucked home a low cross from substitute Lee Clark in injury time to take his season's tally to 22.
Colombian Faustino Asprilla, who did well replacing Peter Beardsley against Everton on Wednesday, made his first start in the Dalglish era at Beardsley's expense.
He was at the heart of many of Newcastle's early efforts, but Les Ferdinand and Shearer squandered clear chances to increase Newcastle's early lead.
Lee almost doubled Newcastle's margin six minutes after the break as Asprilla set him up nicely, but Leicester keeper Kasey Keller tipped away the shot.
Then Leicester turned the game around. Elliott's downward header at the fair post levelled it in the 55th minute and Claridge prodded in the ball five minutes later for a 2-1 lead.
Heskey broke away clear in the 68th minute and it seemed to be over. But Shearer had other ideas.
